results.note: Wikipedia: String Quartet in B minor, composed 1935-36; Barber rewrote the finale (1937) and kept revising it until 1943, when the final form was premiered. aka 'Adagio for Strings' is strictly the orchestral arrangement of the middle movement; kept as a search alias.
Wikipedia: for string orchestra or string quartet, written Dec 1933-Feb 1934; II is Playful Pizzicato. Wikipedia says about 20 minutes, recordings run 16-17; 17 kept.
Wikipedia: composed 1953-54, about 21 minutes, one continuous movement in 17 sections (variations on a basic motif).
IMSLP: String Quintet No. 4, G minor, K. 516, May 1787, 2 violins, 2 violas, cello.
IMSLP: D. 956 (Op. 163), C major, 1828, 2 cellos, average 55 minutes (50 is within tolerance).
IMSLP: String Quintet No. 3, E-flat, Op. 97 (B. 180), 1893, 33 minutes, 2 violas.
IMSLP: G major, Op. 111, 1890, 30 minutes (27 within tolerance), 2 violas.
Composed 1971-72 (premiered Bremen, 6 May 1972), revised 1978 and 1988 (Breitkopf lists 1971/78/88); '1972 (rev. 1988)' is acceptable. Breitkopf duration about 23 minutes.

fixes.notes: String quartet with a tape of recorded speech, train sounds and three pre-recorded quartets; the live players lock to the tape through monitors, with no click track

results.note: Wikipedia: for string quartet and tape, 1988, about 27 minutes; the tape holds speech, train sounds and the 2nd-4th quartets. Performance-practice study of the score: 'No click-track is given, nor is the use of headphones allowed'. The old note's click track and 'live or recorded quartets' were wrong.
Wikipedia: finished January 1983 for Beckett's Company, four movements, about 9 minutes.
Publisher (Dunvagen via Wise Music): 1985, based on the film Mishima, 18 minutes (17 within tolerance); six movements.
IRCAM: Summa for string quartet, 1977-1991, Universal Edition, 5-6 minutes.
UE: Fratres for string quartet, 10 minutes; IRCAM: composed 1977, string quartet version 1989. The 'chords in harmonics' detail was not verified.

G. Schirmer (Wise Music): Five Folksongs in Counterpoint for string quartet, 1951, 18 minutes. Manuscript dated 1951; may have been begun earlier (an earlier three-song 'Negro Folksongs in Counterpoint'), so 'c. 1951' is kept. Movements: Calvary, Clementine, Drink to Me Only with Thine Eyes, Shortnin' Bread, Swing Low Sweet Chariot.

Composer's site: Strum for string quartet/quintet (2006, rev. 2012), 7 minutes; separate version for string orchestra (8 minutes). The chamber version is 'string quartet or quintet' (it began as a quintet).
Composer's note: written 2011 after hearing Haydn's Op. 77 No. 2 minuet and its D-flat trio; c. 11 minutes (string orchestra version 2014).

IMSLP: 1890, revised 1891-92, 35 minutes. Wikipedia: revised Dec 1891-Jan 1892; Adagio theme stated by violin 1, taken up by the cello. Key is D minor (title could read 'String Sextet in D minor, Op. 70 ("Souvenir de Florence")' if the owner wants the key shown).
Wikipedia: Hob. XV:25, 1795, nicknamed 'Gypsy' or 'Gypsy Rondo' trio for its Hungarian-style rondo finale.
IMSLP: 1881-82, 46 minutes; Wikipedia: approx. 47:00, second movement a theme and variations.

IMSLP and Wikipedia: June 1905, E-flat major, 2 violins, viola, cello; both quote 8 minutes (Carl Fischer's figure), but recordings run 7:25-11:09, mostly 9-10 (Emerson 9:02, others 9:04, 9:10, 9:43, 11:09), so 10 is kept.

Scoring, year (dated Friday the Thirteenth, March 1970) and the glasses, maracas and tam-tams are confirmed. Duration: the publisher (C.F. Peters via Wise Music) gives 25 minutes against our 20; a logged concert ran 22:13 and recordings are often shorter. 20 left in place, but 22-25 may be better.

The printed score (Paris: Henry Lemoine, 1989) titles it 'Four, for Tango'; 1988, commissioned by the Kronos Quartet. Duration not checked against a recording (a library record reportedly gives 7:00); 5 kept.

Spanish Wikipedia: lute-quartet original 31 March-6 May 1925, Turina's string quartet version 7-13 May 1925 (string orchestra version Dec 1926). IMSLP and es.wikipedia: about 8 minutes (9 within tolerance).

IMSLP: Novelletten, H. 44, 1904, string quartet, 3 movements (Augener 1915). The violin catalogue gives Bridge's works their Hindmarsh (H.) numbers. Duration not on IMSLP; 12 is in line with recordings.

IMSLP: G. 275, Op. 11 No. 5, 1771, 2 violins, viola, 2 cellos, average duration 22-25 minutes; PTNA gives 23:40 (Amoroso 4:50, Allegro con spirito 8:10, Minuetto 3:10, Rondeau 7:30). 18 was too short. Some editions number the set Op. 13.
IMSLP: G. 324, Op. 30 No. 6, 1780, 2 violins, viola, 2 cellos; exists in two versions (the second with variations on the Ritirata). Duration not on IMSLP; 13 is in line with recordings.
IMSLP: E-flat major, Op. 20, completed 15 Oct 1825, 4 violins, 2 violas, 2 cellos, 32 minutes.
IMSLP: B-flat major, Op. 18, 1859-60, 37 minutes, 2 violins, 2 violas, 2 cellos.
IMSLP: Op. 4, 1899, sextet for 2 violins, 2 violas, 2 cellos, 28 minutes (30 within tolerance).
IMSLP: C major, Op. 7, 1900, 4 violins, 2 violas, 2 cellos, 35 minutes; Wikipedia: completed 1900, about 40 minutes in performance.
IMSLP: K. 502, B-flat, 1786, violin, cello, piano, 3 movements. No duration on IMSLP; 24 is in line with recordings.
IMSLP: C minor, Op. 1 No. 3, 1793-95, 30 minutes, dedicated to Prince Lichnowsky.
IMSLP: Op. 97, March 1811, dedicated to Archduke Rudolph; Wikipedia: third movement (Andante cantabile) in variation form. IMSLP calls it Piano Trio No. 7 if numbering is wanted.

Title, scoring and 40 minutes confirmed (Wikipedia). Year uncertain: Wikipedia says written 1827 and finished 1828; IMSLP gives '1828?'. 1827 left in place. 'The cello opens the slow movement' not checked against the score.
IMSLP: D minor, Op. 49, completed 23 Sept 1839, 28 minutes (30 within tolerance). Wikipedia: piano part rewritten on Hiller's advice, so it is the virtuoso part.
Wikipedia: D minor, Op. 11, written 1846-47 for her sister Rebecka's birthday, published posthumously 1850. IMSLP: 26 minutes, III is 'Lied. Allegretto'.
IMSLP and Wikipedia: G minor, Op. 17, 1846; the finale contains a fugue/fugato. Duration not on IMSLP; 28 is in line with recordings.
IMSLP: B major, Op. 8, 1853-54, revised 1889, 35 minutes for the revision. Wikipedia: almost always played in the revision; opens with a broad theme in cello and piano.
IMSLP: Piano Trio No. 4 'Dumky', E minor, Op. 90 (B. 166), Nov 1890-Feb 1891, 30 minutes; six dumky.
IMSLP: D minor, Op. 32, 1894, in memory of Karl Davydov. Duration not on IMSLP; 26 is in line with recordings.
IMSLP: A minor, M. 67, 1914. Wikipedia: written at Saint-Jean-de-Luz with Basque material; trills, tremolos, harmonics, glissandos. Duration not on IMSLP; 28 is in line with recordings.
IMSLP: Piano Trio, 1921 (Winthrop Rogers, 1928); Wikipedia: entered in Coolidge's 1921 competition. Duration (25) and the 'muted, high writing' were not checked against a source.

note: All 33 composers in this slice are in the violin catalogue with matching spelling; none is in data/chamber/composers.json. Main fixes: Barber quartet is in B minor and was revised until 1943; Different Trains uses no click track (the old note was wrong); Boccherini G. 275 runs about 23 minutes, not 18; Price Five Folksongs 18 minutes (G. Schirmer); Souvenir de Florence revised 1891-92; Bridge Novelletten gets H. 44; Piazzolla's title is 'Four, for Tango'. Doubts: Black Angels duration (publisher says 25), Schubert D. 898 year (1827 or 1828). Durations of several standard piano trios (K. 502, Clara Schumann, Arensky, Ravel, Clarke) could not be checked against a source but look normal.
